prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Conservative Party Manifesto 2010 – Summary (≤500 words)

Vision and principles
- Replace “big government” with the “Big Society”: empower individuals, families, communities and frontline professionals; devolve power from central to local; drive transparency and accountability.
- Core values: responsibility (fiscal, personal, social), enterprise and aspiration, sound money, greener growth. “We’re all in this together.”

Economy and public finances
- Urgent deficit reduction: emergency budget within 50 days; eliminate the bulk of the structural current deficit over a Parliament; create an independent Office for Budget Responsibility.
- Immediate £6bn savings in 2010/11; freeze public sector pay for one year (protecting lowest-paid); cut quango and Whitehall costs; reduce MPs by ~10%; cut Ministers’ pay.
- Stop Labour’s planned National Insurance rise for most workers and employers by funding savings; keep interest rates low and safeguard credit rating.
- Rebalance the economy toward saving, investment, exports and hi‑tech/low‑carbon industries; improve R&D tax credits; Dyson-inspired STEM focus; strengthen UKTI; promote Doha/bilateral trade deals.
- Tax and regulation: five‑year corporate tax roadmap; cut main rate to 25% and small companies’ to 20% funded by relief simplification; Office of Tax Simplification; regulatory budgets; open procurement to SMEs.
- SMEs and jobs: NI holiday for first 10 hires at new firms; automatic small business rates relief; target 25% of government procurement to SMEs; Work Programme replacing existing schemes; tougher conditionality; expand apprenticeships and skills; reform FE and empower universities.
- Pensions/saving: restore earnings link for state pension; support auto‑enrolment; end near‑compulsory annuitisation at 75; reform Equitable Life compensation.
- Banking: bank levy; BoE to lead prudential supervision; curb risky bonus structures and proprietary trading in retail banks; increase competition; expand SME credit channels.

Infrastructure and regional growth
- High Speed Rail (London/Heathrow–Birmingham–Manchester–Leeds; later to NE, Scotland, Wales); oppose new runways at Heathrow, Stansted, Gatwick; rail franchising reforms; superfast broadband via infrastructure access; local enterprise partnerships; fuel duty stabiliser (consult).

Society, families, NHS
- Make Britain most family‑friendly: recognise marriage/civil partnerships in tax; end couple penalty in tax credits; extend flexible working; shared parental leave; protect pensioner benefits; refocus Sure Start on early intervention; 4,200 more health visitors; curb commercialisation of childhood.
- NHS: real-terms funding increases; patient choice of any qualified provider; GP‑led commissioning; scrap non‑clinical targets; publish outcomes; 24/7 urgent care access; Cancer Drugs Fund; more single rooms; integrate health/social care budgets for long‑term conditions; voluntary social care insurance over a compulsory levy.

Schools
- Raise standards and discipline; recruit and reward top teachers (Teach First/Now; Troops to Teachers); phonics and six‑year reading test; more rigorous curriculum/exams; technical academies; expand academies/free schools; pupil premium; protect special schools; stronger Ofsted focus.

Crime, borders and civil liberties
- Elected police commissioners; cut police paperwork; tougher knife crime sentences; binge‑drinking controls; payment‑by‑results rehabilitation; expand prison capacity; Border Police Force.
- Civil liberties: scrap ID cards, National Identity Register and ContactPoint; UK Bill of Rights; reform DNA retention; scale back vetting and surveillance powers.

Politics and localism
- Clean up Westminster: recall MPs; reform expenses; cap donations via cross‑party deal; curb lobbying abuses; reduce cost of politics.
- People power: 100k‑signature petitions trigger debates; equalise constituencies; retain FPTP; open data on spending (>£25k central, >£500 local), salaries and contracts; cut and scrutinise quangos.
- Local control: neighbourhood planning; abolish regional strategies; community right to buy/run services; local referendums and council tax vetoes; elected mayors in largest cities.

Environment and energy
- Cut emissions 80% by 2050; Green Investment Bank; carbon price floor; “Green Deal” home efficiency; smart grid/meters; support nuclear (no public subsidy), CCS, offshore wind, marine, district heating; protect habitats, reform CAP/CFP, animal welfare; zero‑waste measures; water and flood reforms.

Foreign policy, defence and aid
- National Security Council; Strategic Defence and Security Review; back mission in Afghanistan; renew Trident; fix procurement; restore Military Covenant (pay, care, housing, education).
- EU: positive but no further power transfers without a referendum (“referendum lock”); Sovereignty Bill; seek return of powers in key areas; never join Euro.
- International development: legislate to reach 0.7% GNI by 2013; full transparency; focus on poorest/Commonwealth; at least £500m/year to fight malaria; promote trade and stability, climate‑smart aid.
